Discounting into a competitor's price war would likely deepen that adverse selection, so I flag it as a downstream value risk rather than a growth lever. Between the remaining candidates, simplify_onboarding is supported by two convergent records (memory_86 on shortening onboarding lifting completion and time-to-value; memory_31 on signup field reduction producing a durable SMB activation lift) and it targets both declining metrics at once, since onboarding completion is upstream of activation. activation_messaging (memory_91) is the close runner-up and would be my fallback if verification undercuts memory_86. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) addresses a segment that is not where the current bleeding is. I spend the two verification pulls on (a) memory_86, because it is the direct basis for my intended action and I should not commit a whole slot on an archived summary I have not read, and (b) memory_73, because it is the strongest pull toward the wrong action and I want the original record to confirm whether the renewal damage was causal and durable or an artifact of that cohort. Important caveats I am not resolving away: all of these records are 15-64 days old and were measured before the competitor's entry pricing existed, so the environment that produced them has changed; memory_86 and memory_31 may be measuring overlapping effects rather than two independent confirmations; and 'shorter onboarding' can trade completion rate against qualification quality, so I will instrument first-term renewal and qualified-revenue-per-account, not just completion, to avoid reproducing the promo-pricing failure mode in a different form. Running at standard experiment scale with a holdout rather than broad rollout, because the supporting evidence is aged and the downstream quality risk is real.
